issues.issue: Is the appeal moot, and should the court decide the jurisdictional question anyway?
issues.applicant_position: Asks the court to exercise residual discretion and decide the jurisdictional question despite mootness.
issues.respondent_position: Amicus agrees the jurisdictional question is important enough to decide.
issues.result_quote: I am of the view that the issue raised in this appeal is of sufficient importance such that this Court should decide the matter notwithstanding its mootness.

issues.issue: Can a designated judge require evidence for a s.18.1 CSIS Act privilege claim where no s.18.1(4) application was brought?
issues.applicant_position: No: a s.18.1(4) application is the condition precedent to any judicial inquiry into the privilege claim.
issues.respondent_position: Judge has residual power to test privilege claims; absence of prohibitive wording means no ouster.
issues.result_quote: subsection 18.1(4) of the CSIS Act restricts a designated judge’s ability to require evidence in support of a section 18.1 privilege claim where no application has been brought.

issues.issue: May the judge instead order justification to decide whether to appoint an amicus or special advocate?
issues.applicant_position: The Order had no useful purpose; the judge cannot compel justification absent a s.18.1(4) application.
issues.respondent_position: Judge should have jurisdiction to order justification to decide whether an amicus is needed.

issues.issue: Does the court have implied jurisdiction or plenary powers to make the order?
issues.applicant_position: Implied jurisdiction test is stringent; the judge's wish to test the claim is not enough.
issues.respondent_position: Overbroad privilege claims are an abuse of process the judge may address with plenary powers.
issues.result_quote: Accordingly, there is no need to expand on that matter.
